Folks,
Do any of you recall the experiments we did several years ago with the
"TOMI" devices?
The recent comments about the Levitron and Maglev reminded me of an
arrangement of the ring magnets I made which makes a nice demonstration
of a "magnetic track".
I bet a lot of you still have magnets left over from those days, so you
can easily make this.
You will need a total of eight ring magnets. The magnets are to be
bonded together into four pairs. The diagram below shows the final
stacking arrangement. Using a dowel that slips snugly into the center
hole of the magnets, glue each pair togther while held in proper
alignment with the dowel. The magnets will repel each other so I suggest
a thin viscosity, fast curing 'superglue' like adhesive. You can remove
the dowel when the glue has set. When finished you will have three
identical pairs and one opposite pair.
Now its time to have some fun. The pairs of magnets can be arranged as
in the diagram. In this arrangement the pair to the side will orbit the
stack in a VERY stable position at the center.
Of course by orbit I don't mean that it is self propelling, but rather
if you give it a little nudge it will roll around the center of the
stack quite easily.

Hey Keelies:
Recently I read about Teleport Pro in a mail from another mail list.
This program has the ability of mirror copying a whole web site recreating the same
on your hard disk, so that you can browse off-line. I followed an advice to visit the
following site:
http://www.download.com
Then I ran a power scan search for 'browser' and 'off-line'.
Then at one of the first search results appeared Teleport Pro and I clicked to
download it.
I did so by saving the requested site.
After installation of it I tested it on http://www.rqm.ch .
However, I was a little bit too cautious when I configured this session. I asked
Teleport
not to include adjoining links, so I missed a few pages that apparently belonged to
another
department of RQM.
Apart from that, it was a success. I found the press release about the 8.3 over unity
of the
SQM generator in the German branch of the site.
I was really amazed by the performance of Teleport Pro. It automatically finds the
quickest
routes to the requested web site running a number of parallel routes to avoid
congestion.
The speed exceeded that of my Netscape Smart Update by about 50%.
I strongly recommend it. That is the tool we all need when fellow Keelies recommend
web
sites to be checked.
Regards
Niels Stenhoj

Hi Folks!
With regard to increasing mileage using hydrogen;
Got a call from Bruce Mcburney this morning and he is writing a new book
on hydrogen as derived from cracking the water molecule. He said he'd
checked out the Stan Meyers process and it was much more complex than
the HIMAC system and from what he could tell didn't work as claimed by
Meyers.
Bruce thinks this new book will really excite some interest in the HIMAC
system and expressed disappointment because in his opinion, so many
hydrogen researchers fail to mention the cracking of the water molecule
as being a requirement to effective hydrogen production.
I'm not really up on his system so was kind of at a loss, but he has a
lot of confidence in it and says there are many people using it to
radically increase their mileage. I don't recall exactly what he did
but he said he added something to his engine and got a 50% increase in
mileage.
Here in Texas, I understand you can be subject to a fine of something
like $50,000 for changing your carburetion system...correct me if you
have any additional information but it sure puts a damper on wanting to
experiment with it, as much as I like the idea of running water as a
fuel when converted to its component gases.
